newsitem.title: USA: Dole campaign too negative, half of voters say.
newsitem.headline: Dole campaign too negative, half of voters say.

text.p: As Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole considers stepping up attacks against President Bill Clinton to boost his lagging candidacy, a survey released on Saturday shows that nearly half of registered voters think Dole has already been too negative.
In a Time/CNN poll, 49 percent said Dole had engaged in too much negative campaigning, compared to just 22 percent who thought Clinton had attacked his opponents too often.

The same poll of 1,676 registered voters on October 10-11 found that among those likely to vote, 53 percent favored Clinton, 35 percent favored Dole, and seven percent would cast their ballot for Texas billionaire Ross Perot.
Dole has lagged far behind Clinton in recent polls and some of his aides have urged him to increase criticism of Clinton on ethical issues and promote himself as someone Americans can trust.
The final presidential debate next Wednesday would offer Dole his last chance to challenge Clinton directly on ethical issues.
The Time poll found, however, that 40 percent believe Clinton can do a better job of preserving honesty in government, while 39 percent said Dole could do a better job.
The poll has a margin of error of 2.7 percent.
